newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent rebounds after one-year low hit.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent rebounds after one-year low hit.

text.p: Brent crude futures were firmer in late trading on Wednesday, on short covering after prices hit a one year low overnight in London.
July Brent was last traded on SIMEX at $17.62 per barrel, an intraday high after trading as low as $17.50.
July Brent in London on Tuesday fell as low as $17.45, the lowest front month price since May 20, 1996 before settling at $17.50.
"This is purely some consolidation above the low," one broker said.
Brokers said API data was mostly neutral for the market, although the gasoline build ate further into the year-on-year deficit, which could erode a bullish factor that had been supporting gasoline.
Gasoline was last traded on ACCESS at 56.10 cents per gallon, down 0.30 from New York and erasing the overnight 0.20 gain.
NYMEX crude was last traded 13 cents higher at $18.80 compared with New York where prices fell just one cent to $18.67.
